slides.texte_overlay:
habits that separate curious
people from everyone else

they follow the tangent

when a conversation drifts somewhere interesting, they follow it instead of steering back. some of the best things you'll ever learn start as an unplanned detour.

they read the plaque

in museums, parks and old streets, they stop and read the little sign. most people walk past the story, curious people walk away with it in their pocket.

they ask how it works

they wonder how a lift, a fridge or a vaccine actually works, then look it up. ten minutes of curiosity turns everyday objects into small daily wonders.

they feed it daily

they spend 5 minutes every day learning one new thing, on purpose. curiosity is a habit, not a personality trait, and it grows every single time you use it.

they talk to strangers

they ask the taxi driver, the baker or the old man on the bench about their life. everyone knows something you don't, and curious people actually find out what.
